title: Time words
subtitle: now, then, ago, always, twice a week
summary: Say when something happens - now, then or two hours ago - and how often it happens.

lesson.heading: Now, then and ago
lesson.text: **Now** means at this moment. **Then** means at another moment, usually in the past. We use **ago** to say how long before now something happened.

examples.text: I was born in Edinburgh. **Then** we moved to London. **Now** I live in Cambridge.
It is 10 o'clock **now**. I got up four hours **ago**, at 6 o'clock.

lesson.heading: for, from ... to, last and next
lesson.text: Use **for** with a period of time, and **from ... to** with the start and the end. **Last** is the one before now; **next** is the one after now.

examples.text: I lived in Rome **for two years**.
It is July now. **Last month** it was June. **Next month** it will be August.
I saw Ana **last week** and I will see her again **next summer**.

lesson.heading: The past, the present and the future
lesson.text: When we talk about time in general, we talk about **the past**, **the present** and **the future**.

examples.text: **In the past** people didn't have television.
People may travel to Mars **in the future**.
We live in **the present**, in the 21st century.

lesson.heading: Frequency adverbs: how often?
lesson.note: It **always** snows in Russia in winter. It **often** rains in the UK. The Ancient Romans **never** went to America or Australia.

lesson.heading: once a week, twice a day
lesson.text: To say how often something happens, use a number + **a** + a time word. We say **once** for one time and **twice** for two times.

examples.text: I go swimming **once a week**, every Saturday.
I clean my teeth **twice a day**.
I see my uncle **three times a year**.
I play football **four or five times a month**.

lesson.heading: Short time expressions
lesson.text: These four expressions all talk about a short time near now. Learn them together.

examples.text: I'll be with you **in a moment**.

lesson.text: Say **once** and **twice**, not ~~one time~~ or ~~two times~~. From three we use *times*: three times a year.

exercises.prompt: Rosa worked in Hong Kong ___ three years.
exercises.explanation: We use for with a period of time: for three years.

exercises.prompt: ___ the moment Rosa is working in Tokyo.
She was in Hong Kong ___ 2008 to 2011.
exercises.explanation: from 2008 to 2011 gives the start and the end of the time.

exercises.prompt: She was in Hong Kong from 2008 ___ 2011.
exercises.explanation: from 2008 to 2011 gives the start and the end of the time.

exercises.prompt: It is 10 o'clock now. I got up four hours ago. What time did I get up?
exercises.explanation: Four hours ago means four hours before now: 10 - 4 = 6 o'clock.

exercises.prompt: Matthew will get his exam results very soon. When will he probably get them?
exercises.explanation: Soon means in a short time from now.

exercises.prompt: Alice and Adam met for the first time recently. When did they first meet?
I'll help you in a moment. When will I help you?
exercises.explanation: In a moment means in a very short time.

exercises.statement: It always snows in Russia in winter, and it often rains in the UK.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Always means every time; often means many times.

exercises.prompt: We are living in the 21st century. Is each century in the past, the present or the future?
John plays tennis on Mondays and Thursdays. He plays tennis ___.
exercises.explanation: Two times in a week = twice a week.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say how often you see your uncle.
exercises.answer: I see my uncle three times a year.
exercises.explanation: From three we say three times, four times, five times a year.

exercises.statement: The Ancient Romans often went to America and Australia.
exercises.explanation: The Ancient Romans never went to America or Australia. Never means not one time.
